refusedToInherit: The claim that buildForbiddenStrips is the mechanism. Accepted only AFTER a measurement that could have refuted it.
The dispatch's framing that the gap is at a CONVEX joint. It is at a REFLEX joint; convex joints are the safe case. See competingMechanisms below.

competingMechanismsConsideredBeforeTouch.note: ENFORCEMENT: state a second mechanism that would produce the same observation and why it was rejected.

m1_edgeLabelingPicksTheWrongFrontEdge.why_plausible: On a radius street the nearest-road / most-parallel test has to choose among chords of a curve. If it labelled a SIDE edge as front, the street-facing edge would get the 5 ft side setback and the envelope would hug the street -- the exact reported symptom, with the geometry entirely innocent.
m1_edgeLabelingPicksTheWrongFrontEdge.how_rejected: Ran the real labeler on the real ring with the real OSM roads and the real situs. Output: signal=road, confidence 0.851, note 'Street frontage is digitized as 4 contiguous near-collinear segments; the front setback applies along the entire frontage', edges 2,3,4,5 labelled front, insetFeet [5,5,25,25,25,25,5,10,10]. Labeling is CORRECT for this parcel. Rejected on evidence, not on plausibility.

m2_wrongSetbackValues.why_plausible: A wrong front_ft would move the front line without any geometry defect.
m2_wrongSetbackValues.how_rejected: resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks({austin-tx, SF-3}) returned {front 25, side 5, rear 10, side_corner 15}, sourceKind codified-ordinance, 'City of Austin, TX'. Correct. No setback value was changed by this lane.

m3_stripReversalSpikesIsMaskingSomething.why_plausible: It is a draw-time compensation sitting directly on the output.
m3_stripReversalSpikesIsMaskingSomething.how_rejected: It is a pure vertex DELETER: it removes a vertex whose deviation-from-straight exceeds 160 deg AND whose neighbour-to-neighbour mouth is under 0.5 m. It never moves or adds a vertex, so it cannot manufacture an intrusion. It is, however, WHY this survived: see whyThisSurvived.

m4_theBoundaryProbeThatLookedLikeARefuta.what_happened: My first two probes walked the inward normal at the reflex vertex and sampled points along the observed spike leg, testing membership in the strip union with a 1e-6 box. Both reported the wedge FULLY COVERED -- i.e. they REFUTED the mechanism.
m4_theBoundaryProbeThatLookedLikeARefuta.why_they_were_wrong: Both sampled points that lie ON the strip boundary (the spike leg IS a strip edge), and polygonClipping.intersection counts boundary contact as membership. The instrument returned a confident wrong answer.
m4_theBoundaryProbeThatLookedLikeARefuta.how_caught: The answer was CONVENIENT in the wrong direction and disagreed with the pipeline's own observed output, so the instrument was distrusted rather than the result accepted. Replaced with an AREA measurement (difference between the stadium union and the rectangle union, intersected with the parcel), which has no boundary-membership ambiguity.
m4_theBoundaryProbeThatLookedLikeARefuta.lesson: A point-membership test against a boolean union is the wrong instrument for a boundary-anchored sliver. Measure area, or sample interiors.

mechanismEstablished.verdict: CONFIRMED: buildForbiddenStrips is the mechanism, with P-226's convex/reflex wording corrected.
mechanismEstablished.byCodeReading: setbackStrip returned a bare 4-vertex rectangle [a, b, b+n*d, a+n*d]. Its end faces are perpendicular to ITS OWN edge direction. buildForbiddenStrips unions one such rectangle per edge and adds NOTHING at the shared vertices. At a CONVEX vertex of a CCW ring the two rectangles overlap and the corner is covered; at a REFLEX vertex they splay apart and the uncovered wedge has its APEX ON THE PARCEL BOUNDARY. A frontage is reflex exactly when the parcel is on the OUTSIDE of a street curve.
mechanismEstablished.byIndependentMeasurement: forbidden-intersect-parcel computed two ways on 48453:289990 with [5,5,25,25,25,25,5,10,10]: rectangles-only 352.515651 m2, exact stadiums 352.567668 m2. Uncovered 0.052016 m2 in exactly TWO pieces, each with min distance-to-boundary 0.0000 m: a 0.048641 m2 sliver reaching 7.6200 m deep at the frontage (the full 25 ft front setback) and a 0.003375 m2 sliver reaching 1.5240 m at the 5 ft side. The larger piece's vertices coincide with the spike observed in the drawn envelope.
mechanismEstablished.reproducedSymptom: Real pipeline on the real ring: drawn envelope vertex E0 sits exactly on parcel vertex P4; minimum envelope-vertex distance to the front edges = 0.00 ft against a 25 ft front setback.

whyThisSurvived.reason1: The conservation gate cannot see it. conservationFailures derives BOTH of its inputs from buildForbiddenStrips -- inset-intersect-forbidden, and inset area versus the recomputed clip remainder. One party computes both halves, so it is INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, not a meaning-shaped check, and it passes by construction no matter what shape the strips are. It reported healthy throughout.
whyThisSurvived.reason2: stripReversalSpikes catches the NARROW case and was assumed to be the general one. It deletes one vertex per pass and measures the mouth between that vertex's immediate neighbours. The Princeton sliver carries an intermediate vertex on one leg, so at the tip the mouth reads 6.25 m and at the intermediate vertex it reads 7.62 m -- both far over the 0.5 m cap -- and the sliver is preserved.
whyThisSurvived.reason3: Convex joints are the common case and are correct, so most parcels look fine.

planAtCP1.fix: Replace the per-edge rectangle with the exact region {p : dist(p, edge_i) <= d_i}: rectangle plus an inscribed quarter-arc end cap at each endpoint. Definitional, no reflex/convex conditional, no max() over neighbouring setbacks.
planAtCP1.whyRoundAndNotMitre: The ordinance forbids what is within d of the property LINE. Distance-to-segment produces round joins. A mitre forbids points MORE than d from every boundary segment, which the code permits, and is unbounded at a sharp reflex notch.
planAtCP1.whyInscribedAndNotCircumscribed: A circumscribed cap reaches d/cos(halfstep) at the normal direction and would therefore bulge PAST the neighbouring rectangle on a perfectly straight boundary, moving every straight-frontage envelope a few centimetres. Inscribed, the cap is a subset of the true disc and is a provable no-op wherever the rectangles already meet or overlap -- which is precisely what makes falsifier 2 a real test rather than a hope.
planAtCP1.costOfInscribing: worst-case shortfall d*(1-cos(3 deg)) = 0.00137*d, about 1 cm on a 25 ft setback, against a 7.62 m defect.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.whatWouldProveTheWholeCardWrong: If the Princeton envelope's front-edge clearance were already 25 ft before any change, the reported symptom would not be in this function and the repo attribution would be wrong again.

parcelSelectionRule.note: Falsifier 3 requires a SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY chosen curved parcel. Choosing one that looks like the first proves nothing.
parcelSelectionRule.rule: Pulled 869 parcels from a south-Austin bbox off the county service and ranked them by TOTAL REFLEX TURN (sum of right-turn exterior angles on the CCW ring) -- a structural property of the digitization, computed before any envelope was derived and with no reference to my hypothesis about which parcels would fail.
parcelSelectionRule.curvedPick: 48453:284527, 704 Wickford Cir: 44 ring vertices, 17 reflex joints, 170.84 deg total, 0.49 ac. Highest total reflex turn at residential scale.
parcelSelectionRule.straightControl: 48453:285377, 1700 Sylvan Dr: 4 vertices, ZERO reflex joints, 0.23 ac.
